subject: Critical runway triage and two-step rebaseline
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Jensen <sarah.jensen@acme.com>, tom.levy@acme.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 2 Nov 2025 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Critical runway triage and two-step rebaseline

Sarah / Tom —

Thanks again for the sync this morning. After the call we pulled together a concise risk log and an operational recommendation (attached) to get the project back on a defendable track. Key points: 

- Root cause: procurement cadence slipped (vendor PO delayed) + missing infra approvals for the dedicated pool. Combined these created a two-week downstream impact on our planned acceptance window.
- Immediate ask: confirm if the PO can be cleared by COB Wednesday (2025-11-05). If procurement cannot meet that window we need to formally rebaseline the MAP to account for a 14-day buffer.
- Proposed two-step approach: 
  1) Soft rebaseline (internal acceptance dates moved + short-term canary deployment to limit risk) — target owner: Ben Carter — action in 48 hours.
  2) Formal MAP revision (update milestones, procurement gating, and escalation lanes) to be signed off at the Monday governance meeting (2025-11-10).

Attached: runway_risk_log_v1.xlsx (risk register + mitigations), map_snapshot_20251102.pdf (current MAP with highlighted milestones).

Next steps I recommend from Acme: confirm the procurement clearance date and share any internal blockers that will prevent a clean PO sign by Wednesday. From our side we will prepare a rebaseline proposal and a lightweight canary plan to limit downstream impact to acceptance testing.

I’m copying Ben and Laura to coordinate the short-term triage.

Diego Fernandez
Enterprise Sales Director, Redwood Inference
Diego Fernandez | redwood.com

Diego —

Thanks for the quick summary and the risk log. We appreciate the two-step framing. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Procurement update: finance has marked the PO as "in review" — current projected clearance is Friday 2025-11-07 EOD, not Wednesday. I attached the latest PO status snapshot.
- Blockers: our cloud security team still needs the infra diagram and an audit snapshot; without those they won't sign the network exception required for the dedicated pool.
- Can we get the canary plan in writing? We need to share it with security to accelerate the network exception approval.

If Friday is the hard earliest for procurement then we will need the soft rebaseline + canary to avoid hitting the acceptance window.

—Sarah
Sarah Jensen

Diego / team —

I pulled a quick triage plan together based on Diego's risk log and Sarah's procurement update. High level: 

1) Immediate (48 hours): prepare a canary deployment that uses a pre-approved shared pool (short-term) to allow the acceptance test to run without the dedicated GPU pool. That reduces schedule pressure and isolates the procurement dependency. Owner: Laura. ETA: 2025-11-04 17:00 PT.
2) Procurement escalation: Tom (Acme) — please confirm whether finance would accept a revised invoice schedule (split payment) to accelerate sign-off. If not, we need written confirmation that finance finalizes by 2025-11-07 EOD.
3) Contingency: If procurement slips beyond 2025-11-07, we propose a formal 14-day MAP rebaseline with these parameters: 
   - New acceptance start: 2025-11-24
   - Canary window: 2025-11-10 to 2025-11-14 (limited traffic)
   - Escalation lane: Marissa Cole to approve SLA exception for the canary fallbacks.

I booked a 30-minute triage call for Tue 2025-11-04 10:00 PT (calendar invite sent). Please bring procurement confirmation or security checklist status.

Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Team —

Quick recap after this week's triage and the governance sync: 

- Procurement confirmed: PO clearance finalized on 2025-11-07 (Acme finance accommodated a split invoice). Thank you, Tom and Sarah, for the agility here.
- Security: Acme shared the infra diagram; security granted an exception for the dedicated pool pending the canary outcome.
- Decision: Formal MAP rebaseline accepted — new acceptance start is 2025-11-24. The team will run a controlled canary from 2025-11-10 to 2025-11-13 to validate the dedicated pool handover.
- Escalation: Marissa Cole has approved an SLA exception for the canary windows and will own the fallback approval if the canary uncovers regression.

Attachments: rebaseline_proposal_20251105.docx (signed decision record + updated MAP), runway_risk_log_v1.xlsx (updated).

Action items (owners / eta):
- Laura: Canary deployment checklist + runbook by 2025-11-07 12:00 PT.
- Ben: Acceptance test schedule and traffic ramp plan by 2025-11-08 18:00 PT.
- Diego: Follow up on post-canary exec note and finalize procurement closeout by 2025-11-14.

If anything changes on your side (timeline or procurement), flag immediately — we will escalate through Marissa. Thanks for the quick coordination.

Diego Fernandez
Enterprise Sales Director, Redwood Inference
